findings.summary: Cold-offline scan authorization drops signed runtime identity before queue insertion.
evidence: authorizeDecodedScan obtains authorizationByGroup entry (with verified runtimeId) but returns passengerId/passengerLabel/scannedAt/sessionLabel only.
enqueueScan writes deviceId and runtimeId from the returned authorization.runtimeId, which is undefined for every newly authorized cold-offline scan.
Current batch sync maps clientEventId/qrPayload/scannedAt and resolves authenticated runtime server-side, so this does NOT prove all queued scans are unsyncable or an authorization bypass.
createDiscardTombstone uses scan.deviceId as installationRuntimeId; omission loses original signed installation continuity for discard/legacy-closeout attribution.
findings.plan: After explicit release, add behavior regression invoking actual offline authorization/queue path, return signed runtimeId, preserve encrypted QR/AAD/owner/time checks and current cookie-authoritative batch flow.
findings.limits: Source-confirmed omission; no runtime proof executed during this read-only checkpoint and no broad sync-failure claim.

cleared_candidates: Voice preview microphone was not globally blocked: proxy explicitly overrides Permissions-Policy for /ai.
Cold-offline camera replacement race was not proven: cameraStarting prevents a replacement while previous startup remains pending.
Service worker does not cache API/private JSON or arbitrary authenticated navigation.
verification: Read-only physical source and vendor metadata only; no runtime/test edits, services, real scans or provider calls.
